newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti opens 7.4 pct up on Milan bourse.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti opens 7.4 pct up on Milan bourse.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti opened 7.44 percent higher at 780 lire per share on the Milan stock market on Wednesday, following the sudden resignation of chairman Carlo De Benedetti.

Olivetti shares had lost around nine percent over Monday and Tuesday, falling close to all-time lows, before De Benedetti announced his resignation from the post and the company's board late on Tuesday.
Olivetti shares had plunged seven percent to 711 lire (47 cents) per share on Tuesday, close to a record low of 681 hit in late July.
De Benedetti, who said he was stepping down after failing to put the company back in profit this year, is succeeded by board member Antonio Tesone.
Olivetti managing director Francesco Caio remains in the position to which he was appointed in July.
Olivetti, which has not broken even since 1990, announced a first half pre-tax loss of 440.2 billion lire late on Tuesday along with provisions of 200 billion lire for restructuring.
